doc.summary: Runtime chain synthesis from fact-store evidence.
doc.description:
Builds a chain YAML tailored to one host: the shared kill-chain spine
(assign, one-shot scan with reuse, fact refresh, C2 surface, exploit
sweep, session report) plus service-aware steps derived from the
FactStore (gobuster for http, hydra for ssh, enum4linux for smb/rdp) and
an optional playbook binding. Output is validated with
``chain_registry.validate_chain`` before writing, so a generated file
never poisons the registry; the operator owns the file afterwards.

name: synth_chain_data
signature: def synth_chain_data(playbook: str, target: str, services: list[dict], has_creds: bool = False, os_hint: str = '', include_c2: bool = True, techniques: list[str] | None = None) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[str]]

doc.summary: Compose the chain dict for a host; (data, notes).

params.name: playbook
params.description: Playbook token to pin in defaults (enabled: false with '' value).

params.name: services
params.description: Open service dicts with service/port entries.

params.name: has_creds
params.description: Whether credentials exist for the host already.

params.name: os_hint
params.description: OS string from the fact store.

params.name: include_c2
params.description: Whether C2 deploy/loot steps are included.

params.name: techniques
params.description: Optional MITRE technique ids staged as atomic_tests steps.

doc.summary: Pull host facts from the FactStore for synthesis inputs.

returns.description:
{services: [...], has_creds: bool, os_hint: str} — empty services
when nothing about the target is known.

name: synth_technique_chain_data
signature: def synth_technique_chain_data(target: str, techniques: list[str], os_hint: str = '') -> tuple[dict[str, Any], list[str]]

doc.summary: Compose a focused chain of ordered MITRE/atomic technique steps.
doc.description:
Unlike :func:`synth_chain_data`, this produces no scan, C2 or service
spine: it binds the target then emulates each supplied technique in
order as its own ``atomic_tests`` step, so the ChainRunner's shared
EdrPacer applies the configured jitter and sleeper windows between
techniques. Only well-formed technique ids are kept, deduplicated and
uppercased; a bad id can never abort the chain.

params.name: os_hint
params.description: OS string recorded in the chain description.

returns.description:
A ``(data, techniques_used)`` pair. ``data`` is empty with the
reason in ``techniques_used`` when fewer than two valid ids remain.

name: write_generated_chain

doc.description: Invalid data is never written: errors come back instead either way.
